summary.text: A 7-year-old girl diagnosed at 5 years with mixed-subtype morphea (linear, deep circumscribed) presented at diagnosis with hypopigmented macules on the left leg with pruritus and pain. MRI showed deep fascia edema in the lower legs and left leg atrophy, with left ankle and subtalar arthritis. She was negative for antinuclear antibodies and rheumatoid factor, C-reactive protein was mildly elevated, and no skin biopsy was performed.

Initial treatment was intravenous pulse corticosteroids and weekly subcutaneous methotrexate, with mycophenolate mofetil added after 4 months for persistent active disease along with 2 months of oral prednisone. The disease remained active with new areas of involvement after 2 years, so monthly ivIG at 1.69 g/kg/dose for 6 rounds began in September 2023.

She developed aseptic meningitis after the first infusion; later infusions were well tolerated with a saline bolus, acetaminophen, hydrocortisone, rupatadine and a different ivIG brand. PGA-A, LoSCAT, LoSAI and LoSDI decreased during treatment and CXCL9 fell from 1,758 to 941 pg/mL and then to 727 at 8 months on mycophenolate alone.

The benefit was not maintained: four months after stopping ivIG she developed new ankle lesions with increased LoSAI and CXCL9. ivIG was restarted at 1 g/kg/dose, but the second dose was cut short by an urticarial eruption after only 1 full dose, and she is now on tofacitinib.

summary.text: A 10-year-old girl diagnosed at 9 years with linear morphea of the upper limbs first presented with a xerotic patch on the right shoulder that expanded and deepened, with sensitivity on palpation and no pruritus. A skin biopsy at another clinic was read as granuloma annulare, and a second biopsy a year later was consistent with morphea. She had no arthritis or other extracutaneous manifestations.

MRI showed soft tissue indentation of the right upper extremity with vague signal abnormality. Serum antinuclear antibodies (1:640) and anti-double-stranded DNA (34.4) were positive without stigmata of lupus. Three months of pulse intravenous steroids with MMF failed: disease activity persisted with right arm symptoms, waxy induration and elevated C-reactive protein, so ivIG 1 g/kg/dose monthly for 6 months was initiated.

She completed 6 planned ivIG rounds with continued MMF and topical calcipotriol/betamethasone dipropionate, reporting mild nausea after the first 2 doses. Skin improved clearly with no progression after 3 doses, and PGA-A, PGA-D, LoSCAT, LoSDI and CXCL9 decreased after 6 months of ivIG. She remains in remission at the 6-month follow-up.

summary.text: A 13-year-old girl was diagnosed at 10 years with linear morphea of the left arm, reporting no pruritus or pain and an unremarkable medical history. MRI showed tenosynovitis, myositis, fasciitis and osseous involvement, no skin biopsy was performed, and baseline blood tests were within normal limits.

Initial treatment was MMF, two rounds of intravenous methylprednisolone and topical calcipotriol/betamethasone dipropionate. Because of significant gastrointestinal side effects and poor compliance, weekly subcutaneous methotrexate replaced MMF after 3 months; liver enzymes rose transiently, she had nausea, vomiting and missed doses, and MRI after 20 months showed improved osseous involvement while the plaque stayed infiltrated.

She was started on ivIG at 1 g/kg for 6 doses, reporting headache and diarrhea after the first infusion and developing impetigo on the face that cleared with topical mupirocin. Blood work stayed normal; after 6 rounds PGA-A rose from 20 to 30 while PGA-D, LoSCAT, LoSDI, LoSAI and CXCL9 fell, and she remains in remission at 6 months.

Patient 2 text says LoSAI decreased after 6 months of ivIG and that measures stayed relatively stable 2 months after stopping; the Fig 1 plots do not match for some measures, so those two facts are review_only with ambiguities.

Symptoms the source only times after a dose (patient 2 nausea, patient 3 headache, diarrhea, nausea and vomiting) stay in symptoms_function.
The discussion sentence on relapse 4 months after stopping ivIG names only "the patient with longer follow-up"; it is not assigned, and patient 1 relapse is taken from the case text.
